accepted_semantics: Personal advancement belongs only to the actual maker; ordinary FTB party sharing and distinct-team isolation remain unchanged. No personal-task rewrite.
scope: Offline follow-up of pre-prerequisite crafting, later submission, party create/join/leave and normal save/reload; existing Forge and FTB Quests2001.4.22 source plus local jar static references.

state_model.notes: Independent from FTB team selection. Registry advancement and code criterion must still exist.

state_model.state: P[team UUID, task ID]; C[team UUID, object ID]
state_model.notes: Both progression and completion are team state. Completing P/C does not reverse-award H to party members.
Existing keys and ownership retained; proposed four nodes stay rewards:[]. No separate payout ledger.

state_model.persistence: Not serialized as progression; caches start empty and shouldSave starts false in a new TeamData object.
state_model.notes: A change being visible in memory/client synchronization does not alone prove it was marked for disk save.

causal_sequences.scenario: Maker crafts before FTB predecessors are complete
steps: A registered personal code advancement can be awarded directly by the crafting handler without testing FTB prerequisites (current marching-wine bridge is the concrete existing analogue; the four future dedicated receipts are not implemented).
With the current pack progression_mode:linear, FTB playerTick checks canStartTasks before submitTask; incomplete prerequisites stop P/C updates even if H is already true.
A retains H after transferring/consuming the item. Inventory discovery is not a substitute for H.
When a predecessor completes normally through TeamData.setCompleted/setProgress, it clears dependency caches and marks the team dirty.
For LINEAR dependants, Quest.checkForDependantCompletion does not submit their advancement tasks; the next eligible actor's normal submission path performs that step.

AdvancementTask polls every5 game ticks via PLAYER_POST. Once prerequisites are met and A is online in that team, canSubmit reads A's H; AbstractBooleanTask sets team progress1; Task.onCompleted records task completion, then Quest.onCompleted records quest completion.
Quest/chapter iteration is not a topological guarantee. A chain can need a later polling pass; do not require the whole chain to finish in one login callback or assert fixed wall-clock latency.

causal_sequences.scenario: A crafts early, goes offline; B completes the shared prerequisites
steps: A's personal advancement can be saved while the shared child task remains incomplete.
B can complete team prerequisites, but if B lacks H, B's AdvancementTask.canSubmit is false.
The examined FTB callback/polling path evaluates the online submitter's PlayerAdvancements; it does not read offline members' advancement JSON files.
The child can remain incomplete until A returns to this team (or another online member independently has H), after which login submission or the5-tick polling path can submit it.
This is delayed submission with preserved individual history, not permission to award A's history to B.
ServerQuestFile.playerChangedTeam selects the previous and current TeamData from the event.

For personal→party where the joining player is not the party owner, mergeData takes maximum task progress, keeps destination existing started/completed/reward timestamps when IDs overlap, and adds missing entries from the old personal team.
It then calls checkAutoCompletion for quests in the current player context and sends team metadata/full current-team synchronization.
This callback does not scan or merge personal Minecraft advancement histories and does not itself call every advancement task's submitTask.
Subsequent regular player ticks evaluate H against the player's now-current team. Already-completed team tasks skip resubmission.
See conditional cache/save risks FTB-LIFE-R01/R02 below; normal source-flow predictions must not assume merge itself repairs those states.
teamCreated creates/gets TeamData, marks newly created data dirty, sets its team name and adds it to the quest file.
If it is a party team, copyData copies the creator's personal-team progress/completion/rewards/player data/locks into the new party.
The earlier markDirty covers a newly created team's copied state; unlike the existing-party merge case, this path has an explicit dirty mark.
Personal Minecraft H stays with the creator UUID. Newly joining teammates see shared FTB completion without receiving that H.

causal_sequences.scenario: Leave a party and return to one's personal team
steps: ServerQuestFile resolves the prior party and existing personal-team records.
It copies only claimed reward entries matching the destination personal team UUID through mergeClaimedRewards; it does not copy the party's taskProgress or completed map into the personal team.
The personal team's old P/C therefore returns; its old prerequisites may differ from the party's.
A genuine maker's H remains true and can resubmit to the personal team's node when its personal prerequisites permit.
A teammate who never crafted does not acquire H through shared completion. Shared-only progress is not enough to newly submit the personal task after leaving.
Existing completed personal nodes remain completed. The accepted behavior does not reset them.
The reviewed callback has explicit personal→party and party→personal branches; no unconditional assertion is made about administrative direct party→party transfers or absent previous-team events.
Minecraft stores PlayerAdvancements in the player-UUID map. Creating ServerPlayer obtains that object; its constructor loads the UUID JSON. Normal player save/logout calls PlayerAdvancements.save.

PlayerAdvancements.load resolves each saved advancement against the currently registered definitions and reconciles criteria/requirements. Missing advancement IDs are skipped; renamed/deleted criteria are removed by AdvancementProgress.update.

FTB server-start loads quest definitions first and then reads each team SNBT into a new TeamData. It restores task progress, started/completed maps, repeatability, claimed rewards and per-player data, not Minecraft H.
The post-team-login handler resolves the current team, sends definitions/editor state, attaches inventory detection, then visits quests in player context if the team is unlocked.

It handles eligible FLEXIBLE prefilled tasks (not this pack's default), recognizes raw completed quests, checks existing autoclaim rewards, and submits checkOnLogin tasks whose prerequisites allow it.
AdvancementTask inherits checkOnLogin:true because Task.canInsertItem is false and thus consumesResources is false. Its current-player H is checked on this login path.
The normal5-game-tick advancement poll remains the later recovery path when a prerequisite was not yet complete at that quest's position in the login iteration.
FTB world-save/server-stop calls saveNow, which invokes each TeamData.saveIfChanged; only dirty team data is written.
Minecraft advancement JSON and FTB team SNBT are separate saves; the inspected code is not an atomic cross-file craft transaction.
If valid H survives but a team completion was not yet saved, online submission can reconstruct P/C once prerequisites allow it; no recraft is required in the ordinary valid-ID path.
If team C survives but H is missing, team completion does not reconstruct the personal crafting fact. This preserves the agreed maker-only history.

An ordinary save/reload does not prove crash safety. Missing registry IDs, changed criterion names, changed task IDs and corrupt/missing files are separate migration cases; do not overwrite old IDs or use shared completion as a substitute personal receipt.

findings.title: Existing-party merge does not invalidate cached prerequisite results
findings.cause: TeamData.mergeData mutates completed/started/taskProgress maps directly but never calls clearCachedProgress. Its playerChangedTeam caller checks autoclaim and sends synchronization, also without an unconditional server cache invalidation.
concrete_preconditions: Destination party has already cached false for child prerequisites.
Joining personal team supplies those missing completed predecessors.
The child's eligible maker is online, but no other completion/reward/edit event clears the dependency cache after merge.
findings.expected_static_consequence: canStartTasks can continue using cached false and skip the otherwise-eligible advancement submission until another path clears the cache (or data is reconstructed with empty caches). This is a conditional upstream lifecycle risk, not a native reproduced hang.
masking_conditions: A newly granted reward calls markRewardAsClaimed, which clears caches.
Other task progress/completion or explicit cache refresh also clears caches.
A freshly created party starts with fresh caches, so it is not the same setup.
evidence: local installed TeamData.class mergeData and all its lambda references; ServerQuestFile.class lambda$playerChangedTeam$9
findings.action: Record for a later authorized two-player acceptance case. No FTB/Dynasty repair or cache clearing performed.

findings.title: Merge-only progress/reward changes are not independently marked for saving
findings.cause: mergeData and mergeClaimedRewards do not call markDirty or set shouldSave. saveIfChanged only writes when shouldSave is true. The existing-party join/leave callback and server-side sync message construction do not provide an unconditional dirty mark.
concrete_preconditions: Destination TeamData was clean after its previous save.
Join adds progress/completion, or leave adds claimed reward keys.
No later legitimate progress/reward/name/edit change marks the destination team dirty before the save/restart.
findings.expected_static_consequence: The merge can be visible in memory and sent to clients yet be omitted by the next saveIfChanged. Reload can restore the older team snapshot. Maker H may later resubmit progress, but that does not prove every shared completion or merged claimed-reward entry was persisted.
masking_conditions: New-party creation explicitly marks new TeamData dirty before copying.
Unclaimed auto rewards may mark the destination dirty during join.
Any later dirtying activity may incidentally save the merge.
evidence: TeamDataUpdate constructors only read UUID/name; SyncTeamDataMessage constructor/write stores and serializes TeamData; TeamData.write434-485 has no dirty/cache mutation
findings.action: Later acceptance must include clean-destination merge, no unrelated mutations, save/reload, and unchanged existing claimed-reward keys. This batch adds no reward, migration or save workaround.

findings.title: Offline maker history is not eagerly swept by a teammate's prerequisite completion
findings.detail: Normal linear dependants wait for an eligible online submitter's advancement. Requiring immediate completion while only a non-maker teammate is online would contradict the inspected submission mechanism.

findings.title: Party leave restores personal quest progress rather than copying all party completions
findings.detail: Only matching claimed rewards are merged back. The maker's personal advancement allows later valid resubmission; another member's shared-only completion cannot create personal crafting history.

findings.title: Stable advancement ID, code criterion and numeric quest/task IDs are distinct persistence requirements
findings.detail: Minecraft reload resolves advancement definitions and removes unknown criteria; FTB restores numeric keyed maps. Keeping one identity does not compensate for renumbering the other. Existing H/C are not bidirectionally reconciled.

acceptance_cases.scenario: early craft, same team, then ordinary prerequisite completion
acceptance_cases.expected: A's H remains true; team child submits when A next qualifies; no recraft or item retention required.

acceptance_cases.scenario: early craft then A offline, B without H completes prerequisites
acceptance_cases.expected: Child may wait until a qualified maker returns; B must not receive H.

acceptance_cases.scenario: login with valid H and already-complete team prerequisites
acceptance_cases.expected: AdvancementTask is a nonconsuming checkOnLogin task; it can submit during login, with periodic polling as later recovery.

acceptance_cases.scenario: child visited before its final prerequisite in login traversal
acceptance_cases.expected: Allow a later normal polling pass; do not require one topologically ordered login pass.

acceptance_cases.scenario: A joins an existing party with true H but no old task C
acceptance_cases.expected: No H copy; normal current-team submission may create C once party prerequisites allow it.

acceptance_cases.scenario: B joins party where A already completed the child
acceptance_cases.expected: B sees shared C but H[B] remains false.

acceptance_cases.scenario: A leaves party, personal prerequisites incomplete
acceptance_cases.expected: H[A] survives; personal child waits for personal prerequisites.

acceptance_cases.scenario: B leaves with only party-shared completion
acceptance_cases.expected: Old personal C returns; shared C alone must not award H[B] or create a personal crafting receipt.

acceptance_cases.scenario: clean existing party with cached-false prerequisite, import the missing predecessor
acceptance_cases.expected: Exercise R01 without unrelated cache-clearing progress/reward events.

acceptance_cases.scenario: clean destination, merge only, save/reload without extra progress/rewards
acceptance_cases.expected: Exercise R02; verify imported P/C and existing reward-claim keys survive.

acceptance_cases.scenario: maker H saved, team C missing
acceptance_cases.expected: Re-submit from H once eligible; do not trigger a second custom payout.

acceptance_cases.scenario: team C saved, maker H missing
acceptance_cases.expected: Do not infer/regrant H from shared C; investigate persistence/identity separately.

acceptance_cases.scenario: normal reload with stable IDs; variant item already consumed
acceptance_cases.expected: History is independent of held item; no inventory-based reconstruction needed.

acceptance_cases.scenario: old completed IDs and claimed rewards across join/leave/reload
acceptance_cases.expected: Preserve existing keys and intended team/per-player semantics; no new rewards added for this audit.

evidence.method: Official source causal reading cross-checked with a non-executing Python classfile constant-pool/instruction reference decoder. This is not a JVM run, full control-flow proof or multiplayer reproduction.
limits: No original saves opened and no in-memory server objects created.
Four future dedicated variant advancement/task implementations still do not exist; lifecycle predictions assume the accepted registered personal-advancement design.

No complete audit of every third-party event listener or FTB Teams internal membership dispatch. Causal traces start at the inspected FTB Quests callbacks and use their stated event branch conditions.
Conditional merge risks can be masked by unrelated dirtying/cache-invalidating mutations; no unconditional loss or duplicate-reward exploit claimed.
Dynamic datapack reload/crash consistency is not accepted by normal save/reload source inspection.
Bounded source ranges only; no whole-package or1000-reference credit.
